symptom: `create microflow M.F () returns M.Enum as $V` (also nanoflow and rule) passed `check -p --references` and was then refused by exec with "entity 'M.Enum' not found for return type"; for a rule check refused it too, with a misleading "a rule must return a Boolean or an enumeration, not Entity". `returns enum M.Enum`, `Enumeration(M.Enum)` and a bare enum name as a PARAMETER type all worked
cause: the parser records a bare Module.Name as an entity reference; the create handlers retry it as an enumeration for parameters but their return-type block only looked for an entity, while declaredTypeResolver.check was written against the general rule (entity or enumeration) and validateRule saw the unretyped entity kind
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_build.go` (microflow and nanoflow build), `mdl/executor/cmd_rules_create.go`, `bareEnumerationType` in `cmd_microflows_helpers.go`, `declaredTypeResolver.bareEnumeration` and the rule case in `validate.go`
insight: A fallback added for one declaration site (parameters) but not its sibling (return types) is a check/exec disagreement, because the checker was written against the general rule, not the site. When a handler resolves a name in one place, grep for the same lookup at every sibling site before trusting a green `check -p`; and a check-time validator that reads the AST kind (validateRule: Boolean or enumeration) needs the same retyping exec applies, or it refuses what exec now accepts. Settled by a PedApp assertAgree test per kind plus a stored-BSON comparison against the `enum` spelling, and mx check 11.12.5 at 0 errors. The same ambiguity is still open for a Java action's bare enum parameter and return type, which stores an entity type (CE1613)
